newsitem.title: ITALY: No taxes, pension block in Italy budget - Bertinotti.
newsitem.headline: No taxes, pension block in Italy budget - Bertinotti.

text.p: The forthcoming mini-budget will include some 16 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures but there will be no new taxes or block on people taking retirement, the leader of the hardleft Communist Refoundation said.

Speaking to reporters after a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and coalition allies, Refoundation's Fausto Bertinotti said around a third of the money would come from advance taxes on company severance funds.

A further third would come from a reduction in spending by certain state funds while the rest of the cash would be raised by fiscal measures such as new methods of collecting inheritance tax and other levies.
The budget, needed to get the economy back on track for the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999, is expected to be introduced by the cabinet on Thursday.
Bertinotti said the government planned to save money this year by holding back end-of-contract severance payments to state workers for six months.
In addition it would ask companies for payment of taxes on severance funds, two years ahead of schedule.

Firms use the funds as a cheap source of self-financing and have protested bitterly over earlier reports that the government was planning to suck some of this cash out of the system. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
